title: Capability
description: Schema for a capability artefact produced by the Discovery Team. A capability is a distinct area of institutional responsibility and the deployment boundary for a self-contained domain.

id.description: Unique capability identifier in the format CAP-NNN

name.description: Short human-readable name for the capability

description.description: What this capability is and why the organisation must have it

mandate_source.description: Legislation, regulation, or policy that mandates or constrains this capability

market_context.description: Market research findings that informed the capability design — competitive landscape, regulatory horizon, build-vs-buy assessment, and revenue model

competitive_landscape.description: Who does what in the market, what is table stakes vs differentiator, what is being unbundled or re-bundled

table_stakes.description: Capabilities that every major player offers — minimum viable product

differentiators.description: Capabilities where leading players achieve genuine competitive advantage

disruptors.description: Technology-led or specialist entrants reshaping the market

unbundling.description: Sub-capabilities being unbundled by specialists or fintechs

rebundling.description: Sub-capabilities being re-bundled by platform players or neobanks

switching_drivers.description: Primary drivers of customer switching between providers

regulatory_horizon.description: Current and upcoming regulation that creates or constrains this capability

incoming_2_3_years.description: Regulation expected within the next 2-3 years that will reshape this capability

enforcement_signals.description: FCA/PRA enforcement actions or supervisory statements indicating regulatory focus areas

build_vs_buy.description: Assessment of what platform options exist and what must be built in-house

platform_options.description: SaaS, BaaS, or platform providers that could deliver parts of this capability

must_build_in_house.description: Sub-capabilities or components that must remain in-house for regulatory or strategic reasons

buy_candidates.description: Sub-capabilities that are strong buy or partner candidates

revenue_model.description: Where the margin sits and how this capability is commercially sustained

primary_revenue_streams.description: Main sources of income from this capability

margin_pressure.description: Forces compressing margin in this capability

cross_sell_hooks.description: Cross-sell or upsell pathways this capability enables

sub_capabilities.description: Subdivisions of this capability, each evaluated against the promotion test

id.description: Sub-capability identifier in the format CAP-NNN.XX

promotion_test.description: Four-criterion promotion test. If 3+ criteria met the sub-capability is promoted to standalone capability.

distinct_participants.description: Does this sub-capability involve participants not present in the parent? (e.g. specialist third parties, separate regulators)

separate_regulatory_framework.description: Is this sub-capability governed by a distinct regulatory framework separate from the parent?

distinct_lifecycle.description: Does this sub-capability have end-to-end phases that do not map onto the parent capability's lifecycle?

independent_scalability.description: Does this sub-capability have demand drivers or scaling requirements that are independent of the parent?

criteria_met.description: Number of promotion criteria met (0-4). Threshold for promotion is 3.

decision.description: RETAIN: stays inside the parent capability's deployable unit. PROMOTE: becomes an independently deployable capability.

market_evidence.description: Market research findings that support or challenge the promotion decision — specialist providers, distinct regulation, distinct product lifecycle, independent demand drivers

design_decisions.description: Non-obvious design choices made during capability modelling with rationale and alternatives considered
